prompt: Create one ambitious original editorial illustration for a proposed Field Notes section header on Code Like It's 198x, a computing education website. Preview artwork only, not a historical document or photograph. Wide panoramic 3:1 composition. An imagined retro-computing investigation workbench seen as a dramatic oblique paper cutaway: on the left, folded graph paper with deliberately abstract, unlabelled waveform marks, pencil corrections and translucent tracing-paper layers; on the right, an anonymous beige 1980s-style keyboard edge, loose unbranded circuit board fragments, a few chunky pixels emerging from the page and a magnifying glass catching warm light. A thin rust-red thread loosely travels between the paper and electronics, suggesting an investigation without an explicit diagram or network. Warm off-white paper ground, rich charcoal ink, restrained burnt-orange spot accents, subtle muted green electronics. Beautiful printed editorial art with analogue texture, convincing shadows, carefully composed overlaps, generous quiet cream-paper central-left area for a future live heading. Elements break across imagined margins; no boxed tiles, no rounded panels, no artificial UI. Evoke curiosity and making sense of a bug, not generic cyberpunk. No people, no faces, no logos, no readable text, no code, no invented factual diagrams, no title embedded in art. All marks are abstract and decorative. Full bleed at edges. Visually sophisticated and tactile, with strong silhouette and deliberate restraint.
